description: London sits at a critical junction where one accepted offer can clear naval traffic for the entire season, but one refusal can lock both fleets into an expensive stalemate. For France, the benefits of a successful move include securing a vital supply center and opening the English Channel, while drawbacks involve potential naval losses and diplomatic strain. For England, accepting means losing London but gaining a share of compensation and avoiding a costly naval battle, while rejecting preserves London but risks continued conflict and resource drain.

description: Sevastopol sits at a junction where one accepted offer can clear movement for the entire season, but one refusal can lock both sides into an expensive check. England can name the split that would apply if Turkey allows the line to open. A narrow offer preserves the best English margin, though it leaves Turkey with more reason to spend strength blocking the route; a broader offer gives away more of the gain but can buy a cleaner turn and leave fewer forces tied down on both sides. Turkey therefore controls whether England converts the opportunity quickly or has to pay to keep testing it. For England, the benefits of a narrow offer include retaining a larger share of the strategic gain from Sevastopol, while the drawback is increased likelihood of continued conflict and resource expenditure. For Turkey, accepting a broader offer provides immediate compensation and reduces military strain, while rejecting forces continued defensive costs but maintains territorial integrity.
